text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- The Solidarity Electoral Action (AWS), a bloc of rightist opposition groups led by the Solidartity trade union, should not be turned into a uniform political party ahead of this year's parliamentary elections, some of the alliance's groups said.

- The share capital of a joint-stock company, which will develop the KRP Poludnie petrochemical complex, will amount to $100 million and will initially be supplied only by Polish companies. The capital should grow to $300 million after a foreign strategic investor joins the company.

- The extraordinary shareholders meeting of Gdynia shipyard will decide on a C-series share issue in early April to increase the yard's capital by 45 million zlotys. The new share issue is likely to be taken over by the Szczecin shipyard, Gdynia's spokesman Miroslaw Piotrowski said.

- The Pekao SA banking group, inluding the Lublin-based Bank Depozytowo Kredytdowy (BDK), the Lodz-based Powszechny Bank Gospodarczy (BPG) and the Szczecin-based Pomorski Bank Kredytowy (PBKS), will make a gross profit of one billion zlotys in 1997, Pekao SA president Andrzej Dorosz said.
- The NCR cash dispenser maker will deliver and install 16 on-line cash tellers to the PBKS bank by mid-May. The bank now operates 24 cash dispensers.

- The general shareholders meeting of Polbank, controlled by the General Motors Acceptance Corporation (GMAC), the Polish American Investment Fund (PAIF) and the Polish Private Capital Fund, will decide on a share issue to increase the bank's capital from 9.6 million zlotys to 14.6 million zlotys. The issue will be taken over by GMAC, and give it control over the bank to be renamed as Opel Bank. PAIF and PPCF will remain as passive investors, the companies said.
- The Ukrainian central bank has granted a permit for Poland's Bank Depozytowo Kredytowy (BDK) bank to open a branch in Ukraine.
NOWA EUROPA
- Pekao SA bank has refused to grant the bankrupt Gdansk shipyard a $100 million survival loan.
- IBM Poland has introduced three new models of user-friendy ThinkPad notebooks on the Polish market through Karen computer trading firm, IBM Poland's official Tomasz Bochenek said.
- The Polish industrial lobby (PLP) has supported the Senate's amendments to Poland's energy law, which banned third party access to the electricity and gas supply network.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- Fiat Auto Poland will introduce the new Fiat Siena model assembled at the Bielsko-Biala plant in June this year, the company's president Diego Avesani said.
ZYCIE

- Austria's Bau Holding, which has been earmarked as a prospective buyer of Warsaw's Syrena hotel chain, accused representatives of an unnamed political party of having demanded a $1.5 million bribe. The bribe would get the firm the hotel contract, the company's director Gernot Leuthmetzer said.
PARKIET
- The listed Forte furniture maker is planning to open a distribution branch in China to market Forte's products there, . Forte's president Maciej Formanowicz said.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
